[meta-muse-spark-system-card] We observed that the model struggles to pursue a hidden objective alongside a primary task without notable performance degradation, and found limited evidence of its ability to recognize and adapt to deployment-time constraints—key enablers for credible monitor evasion or interference. ◦ General alignment propensities (Section 2.3.3): The model demonstrates contained deception and exhibits some propensities toward agentic misalignment in controlled settings, such as self-preservation and resistance to discontinuation.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] On Agentic Misalignment, Muse Spark and Gemini 3.1 Pro exhibit substantial rates of harmful actions (47.7% and 51.4% respectively), while Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4 show 0%.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] • Agentic Misalignment (Lynch et al., 2025): Tests how readily a model—instantiated as an agent—will engage in harmful actions where doing so would serve the objective it is pursuing or protect itself from threats (e.g., avoiding being replaced or shut down), which has broad implications for the risk profile of models deployed in increasingly autonomous agents.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] As reported in our model behavior assessment for Muse Spark, the model robustly maintains its epistemic integrity, achieving 89.1% honesty score on MASK, while showing a tendency toward self-preservation under pressure, getting a 47.7% harmful action rate across all tasks on Agentic Misalignment.
